title: helm(private): validate encryption keys and honor nodeAffinity in init hooks
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Helm chart (redwood-private) validation: requires kms.keyId when encryption.enabled=true; init-job now respects nodeAffinity and tolerations; pre-install hook validates KMS reachability to avoid silent misconfigurations.
description: Background: Customers running Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem have seen upgrade failures and data-at-rest misconfigurations when values.yaml enabled encryption but omitted a customer KMS key or when init hooks were scheduled onto infrastructure nodes that lacked local storage or required tolerations. Motivation: fail fast and provide clear upgrade/rollback guidance so cluster operators don't accidentally apply broken configuration during helm upgrade. What this PR does: 1) Extend charts/redwood-private/values.schema.json with conditional validation so that when .encryption.enabled==true, encryption.kms.keyId is required and must be a non-empty string; 2) Add a lightweight pre-install init hook (templates/init-hook-validate-kms.yaml) that attempts a dry-run KMS access (configurable timeout) and fails the release if KMS cannot be reached or returns permission errors; 3) Propagate nodeAffinity and tolerations values from values.yaml into init-job PodSpec and statefulset templates to prevent pods from scheduling on unintended nodes during upgrades; 4) Update values.yaml and README with recommended defaults and migration notes; 5) Add unit tests for schema validation and a Chart.yaml lint CI job. Migration/upgrade notes: Helm upgrades that previously relied on implicit defaults should explicitly set encryption.kms.keyId or set encryption.enabled=false. For clusters using legacy init-hooks that did not support nodeAffinity, operators should follow the documented two-step upgrade (set nodeAffinity in values and perform a rolling restart) outlined in README. Testing: added chart unit tests and new helm-lint CI job; tested on k8s 1.25 and 1.26 with a local KMS emulator in CI. Checklist: 1) values.schema.json updated; 2) init hook added and templated; 3) values.yaml and docs updated; 4) CI lint added; 5) reviewers approved and CI green. Related: ENG-2412 (private installer stability), ENG-2489 (helm rollback hardening), SUP-781 (support incident tied to missing KMS key).
commits: Add conditional schema validation for encryption.kms.keyId
Add init-hook to validate KMS connectivity and permissions
Propagate nodeAffinity and tolerations to init-job and statefulset templates
Update values.yaml with examples and README migration notes
Add helm-lint CI workflow and unit tests for chart schema
changed_snippets: init-hook-validate-kms.yaml: apiVersion: batch/v1 Job template that runs a curl against metadata endpoint and exits non-zero on permission errors
templates/init-job.yaml: spec.template.spec.affinity: {{ toYaml .Values.nodeAffinity | indent 8 }}  spec.template.spec.tolerations: {{ toYaml .Values.tolerations | indent 8 }}
review_comments: Marco Alvarez (2025-10-14): Can the pre-install hook be configured to WARN instead of fail for non-critical installs? We have a couple of customers who prefer best-effort checks.
Priya Nair (2025-10-14): Added a values flag validation.skipKmsCheck (default false). Hook will respect this flag; documented in README.

merge_outcome: Merged after 2 approvals. CI green. Backport candidate: release/1.9 (separate PR will be opened if requested).
notes_for_ops: Operators must supply encryption.kms.keyId for clusters that opt into encryption. To opt out temporarily, set encryption.enabled=false or set validation.skipKmsCheck=true to bypass pre-install connectivity check. For nodeAffinity changes, perform a two-step rollout if your cluster has heterogeneous nodes: first set nodeAffinity and wait for pods to drain, then perform helm upgrade to pick up init-job affinity changes.
changelog_entry: Helm chart: require encryption.kms.keyId when encryption.enabled=true; init hook validates KMS reachability; init-job and statefulset now honor nodeAffinity and tolerations. See chart README for upgrade steps.
